_purpose: EWG's Shopper's Guide to Pesticides in Produce - annual, based on real USDA residue testing (not the reasoning-from-first-principles approach used for peanut_butter in category_facts.json). Use this for any FRESH PRODUCE category going forward: look up the item here first before hand-deriving organic reasoning. Only covers fruits/vegetables - does not include nuts, grains, legumes, dairy, meat, or packaged/processed goods.
source: EWG 2026 Shopper's Guide to Pesticides in Produce
source_note: EWG's own site (ewg.org) blocks automated fetches (403) - this was compiled from a secondary source mirroring their published 2026 data on 2026-09-09. Re-verify against ewg.org directly if precision matters, and re-fetch next year - this list updates annually.
weight_reasoning: Dirty Dozen items have real measured high pesticide residue (96% of samples test positive) - a stronger evidence grade than the peanut_butter exposure-pathway argument, so a higher weight than peanut_butter's is defensible if this framework is used. Clean Fifteen gets 0 (badge-only, same treatment as peanut_butter) since ~60% of samples show no detectable residue at all - buying organic doesn't meaningfully change exposure. 'not_listed' is null on purpose: an item EWG hasn't tested isn't evidence either way - don't default it to any weight, research it specifically like peanut_butter was, or leave at badge-only until you do.
